summary: Backend-only testing of 4 workflow features from iteration 109. All 12 pytest tests PASSED (100%). Verified: (1) Assignment conflict validation raises 409 ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT with correct detail payload in both directions (org→facility exists and facility→org exists), and does NOT raise when reporting_period differs. (2) Delete approval workflow: deleting an approved record on an assignment with requires_approval=True correctly creates an approval_request with request_type='delete', marks the record with pending_deletion=True, and does NOT hard delete. Approving the delete request via ApprovalWorkflowService.make_decision then hard-deletes the record. Without approval workflow, delete_record still performs immediate hard delete. (3) Resubmission rule: updating a rejected record raises HTTPException 400 REJECTED_RECORD_EDIT_NOT_ALLOWED at both the service layer and via PUT /api/esg-records/records/environment/{id}. (4) Aggregate approval status: pure function calculate_aggregate_approval_status returns ALL_APPROVED, HAS_REJECTION (even with mix), PARTIALLY_APPROVED (3 approved + 2 pending), ALL_PENDING, and NOT_REQUIRED (empty) exactly per spec.

minor.issue: Outer try/except Exception at router.py L883-884 wraps ALL exceptions (including HTTPException) into a generic 500 error. This means the 409 ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT raised by _validate_no_assignment_conflict will be returned to API clients as HTTP 500 with detail=str(e) instead of the intended structured 409 payload. Should re-raise HTTPException without wrapping (except HTTPException: raise / except Exception: ...).

minor.endpoint: POST /api/esg-records/assignments (facility-level with existing org-level, or vice versa)
minor.issue: The endpoint short-circuits into replace_org_with_facility_assignments / replace_facility_with_org_assignment for cross-level switches, silently DELETING the previously conflicting assignments before creating the new one. This effectively bypasses the 409 ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT protection at the API layer — callers never see the conflict error even though the service layer validation exists. If the intent is to truly block conflicts, the endpoint should reject rather than auto-replace; if auto-replace is desired, the ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT check is only reachable via internal code paths.

Order of operations: _validate_no_assignment_conflict runs BEFORE the existing-assignment lookup. For facility-level updates, the duplicate check on line 150-164 will match the very record being updated and raise 409 DUPLICATE_ASSIGNMENT. This makes the 'update existing' branch on line 207 effectively unreachable for facility-level assignments via this method. Recommend either skipping the duplicate check when the match IS the assignment being upserted, or running the validator only on true create (after the existing lookup).

Router (router.py L474) does `if not deleted: raise 404`. But service.delete_record now returns a dict like {'status': 'pending_approval', ...} which is truthy in all cases including 'not_found'. So a 404 case will be returned as 200 with body {'message': 'Record deleted', 'record': {'status': 'not_found', 'message': 'Record not found'}}. Also, when status='pending_approval' the API still returns the misleading message 'Record deleted' even though nothing was deleted. Router should inspect result['status'] and return appropriate HTTP status/message.

On DELETE approval, task revert query uses task_query = {organization_id, category, period_key, [subcategory, facility_id]}. This lacks sub_subcategory filter, so it may revert unrelated tasks that share category/subcategory but differ in sub_subcategory.

action_items: Fix POST /api/esg-records/assignments to re-raise HTTPException so 409 ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT reaches clients instead of being masked as 500.

Decide semantics of cross-level assignment creation: either surface 409 (and drop the replace_*() short-circuits) or drop the conflict validator — currently both exist and the endpoint bypasses the validator.
In assignment_service_v2.create_or_update_assignment, skip DUPLICATE_ASSIGNMENT check for the row being upserted (or move conflict validation after the existing-assignment lookup so updates work).
Fix DELETE /api/esg-records/records/{section}/{record_id} router to differentiate {status: 'pending_approval'} vs 'not_found' vs successful delete and return appropriate HTTP status codes/messages.
Add sub_subcategory to task revert query in approval_workflow/service.py delete-approval branch.
critical_code_review_comments: completion_service.py L124-181 calculate_aggregate_approval_status: correct and well-documented. Rejection precedence honored.
assignment_service_v2.py L76-164 _validate_no_assignment_conflict: correct logic and detail payloads; but see minor issue about duplicate check running before existing-lookup.

esg_records/service.py L1147-1156: delete_record correctly branches on assignment.requires_approval AND record.approval_status=='approved' — behavior aligns with spec (only approved records trigger delete-approval flow; drafts/rejected records can be deleted immediately). Well-designed.

esg_records/service.py L1213-1215: when no approver_id/approval_chain, delete falls through to immediate hard delete — reasonable fallback but should log a warning since requires_approval was set but no approver configured.
esg_records/router.py delete_record endpoint (L454-477): does not consume the new dict return shape from service. Will report success even on not_found. High-impact for UX.
esg_records/service.py L760-774 update_record: rejection guard is clean and returns full detail (rejection_reason, rejected_at). Good UX.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral: each test inserts TEST_-prefixed docs into esg_assignments / environment_records / approval_requests via pymongo sync client and cleans up in finally blocks. No permanent data left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter109_workflow_features.py uses a single shared asyncio LOOP (module-level) + sync pymongo for setup/cleanup because motor's client is bound to the first event loop it sees. Do NOT convert these tests to @pytest.mark.asyncio without also pinning event_loop scope to session — pytest-asyncio 1.3 STRICT mode uses per-test loops which breaks motor.
rca of the issue: N/A — all 4 features work as specified at the service/pure-function layer. However, note that ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT (409) is NOT exposed via the public POST /api/esg-records/assignments endpoint due to (a) the endpoint's own replace_*() short-circuits that delete existing conflicts, and (b) a bare `except Exception` at router.py L883 that converts any HTTPException into 500. E1 should decide whether the API should surface 409 or continue the auto-switch behavior.
